title: Manifest
description: The complete pipeline manifest parsed from manifest.toml.

defaults.description: Default values applied to all steps unless overridden.

message.description: Error message shown when constraint is violated

category.description:
Free-form label for grouping failures across runs, e.g. `quality`, `network`.

Deliberately unconstrained and never interpreted: nothing in the engine branches on it, so a fixed vocabulary would only reject labels a vendor's dashboard finds useful.

exit_code.description: Process exit code that signals this error (author band: 1..=63, unique). A step exits with this code to report the error; the engine maps it back.

max_retries.description: Max retries for this error type (overrides step-level retries)

retryable.description: Should the step be retried on this error?

oneOf.description: Error condition, step fails but pipeline may continue

GroupDef.description: Parameter group definition for UI organization.

ParamDef.description: A parameter definition from the manifest.

readonly.description: If true, user cannot override via -p or -c. Value is resolved normally (base default → profile override).

on_failure.description: Scripts to run after any step fails

on_start.description: Scripts to run before any steps execute

on_success.description: Scripts to run after all steps complete successfully

cache_dir.description:
Directory name, relative to `WORK_DIR`, holding results shared across runs.

Required for any step that sets `cache = true`. Declared once at the pipeline level rather than per step so every cached step lands in one place a user can inspect or delete, and so the name is a property of the pipeline rather than a detail repeated at each use.

min_threads.description: Minimum number of threads required to run this pipeline.

profile.description: Pipeline-defined profile for profile-specific parameter defaults.

requires.description:
External tools and libraries the pipeline's steps invoke.

Advisory metadata: declaring a requirement does not install it, and nothing is checked during a run. `flowrs inspect --check-environment` reports what is missing, on the machine that will actually execute the steps. Activating whatever provides them — a module system, a conda environment, a container — stays the operator's job; FlowRs only inherits `PATH`.

Profile.description:
A pipeline-defined profile that drives profile-specific parameter defaults.

The profile references a param (which should have `enum` values defined), provides a detector script for auto-detection, and maps values to profiles.

detector.description: Detector script path relative to `bin/` directory.

param.description: Name of the parameter that acts as profile (must exist in `[params]`).

profiles.description: Maps profile names to their member values. e.g., `{ "ngs": ["SINGLE", "PAIRED"], "tgs": ["TGSONT", "TGSPACBIO"] }`

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the detector script before failing. Defaults to `DEFAULT_DETECTOR_TIMEOUT_SECS`. Set higher for detectors that scan large datasets or access slow/remote filesystems.

unassigned_ok.description:
Permit enum values of the profile param that belong to no profile.

By default every enum value must be assigned to exactly one profile: a value in none is detectable but selects no profile, so the run silently uses base defaults for every profile-specific param — the author's `[params.X.ngs]` blocks simply do not apply, with nothing saying so.

Set this when that is intended, e.g. a value handled entirely by base defaults. It relaxes the manifest check only; detection of an unassigned value still **warns** at run time, naming the value and the fallback. The escape hatch is for authors who accept the behaviour, not a way to silence the report of it.

Requirements.description:
External tools and libraries a pipeline needs, grouped by how presence is established.

Three groups rather than one list with a `type` field: each is probed by a different mechanism (a `PATH` lookup, an interpreter import, a loader query), and the TOML reads as the sections a pipeline author already thinks in.

Versions are deliberately absent. A constraint is only worth writing down if it can be checked, and there is no portable way to ask an arbitrary bioinformatics tool its version — `samtools --version`, `bwa` with no argument, and `fastqc --version` disagree on both the flag and the format. Recording constraints that are never enforced would be worse than recording none: it reads as a guarantee. Presence is what FlowRs can honestly check, so presence is what the schema expresses.

python.description:
Python modules that must import, e.g. `["numpy", "pysam"]`.

Import names, not distribution names: `Bio`, not `biopython`.

r.description: R packages that must load, e.g. `["ggplot2", "dplyr"]`.

tools.description: Executables that must resolve on `PATH`, e.g. `["samtools", "bwa"]`.

StepDef.description: A single step in the pipeline workflow.

cache.description:
Reuse this step's results across runs when its inputs are unchanged.

A cached step writes to `${CACHE_DIR}`, a directory keyed by everything that can change its output (see `cache_key`). When a run finds a completed entry for that key it skips the step and downstream steps read the existing results.

cache_key.description:
Parameters whose values are part of this step's cache identity.

Only these participate — deliberately not every resolved param. Hashing all of them would invalidate a QC step because an unrelated downstream threshold changed, which defeats the point of caching. Declaring the list is the author's statement of what this step actually reads.

The step's executable content and the identity of its cached upstreams are always included, so editing a script or invalidating an upstream invalidates this step without anything being declared here.

depends_on.description: Step names that must complete before this step

exec.description: Executable filename relative to pipeline's steps/ directory

outputs.description: Expected output files this step should produce (optional). Paths must use allowed variables: ${OUT_DIR}, ${WORK_DIR}, ${TMP_DIR}, and ${CACHE_DIR} for a cached step. If declared, FlowRs will check these files exist after step completion. Missing required outputs convert a successful exit (0) into a failure.

retries.description: Number of retry attempts on failure (0 = no retries).

retry_delay.description: Delay in seconds between retry attempts.

shared.description: If true, executable lives in a shared location rather than the pipeline's steps/

teardown.description: If true, this step runs after the main pipeline completes (success or failure).

threads.description: Thread allocation: "auto" (use CLI value) or fixed number.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Step is killed if it exceeds this duration.

trigger_rule.description: Trigger rule determining when this step should execute

StepDefaults.description: Default values applied to all steps unless overridden at the step level.

retries.description: Default number of retry attempts for all steps.

retry_delay.description: Default delay in seconds between retry attempts.

timeout.description: Default timeout in seconds for all steps.

ThreadAllocation.description: Thread allocation: the string "auto" to use the CLI-provided thread count, or a fixed thread count.

TriggerRule.description: Trigger rule determining when a step should execute.

oneOf.description: All upstream tasks must complete (any state)
At least one upstream task must succeed
At least one upstream task must fail
No upstream tasks failed (success or skipped OK)
No failures and at least one success
Always execute regardless of upstream states
